chunks: Muḥammad ibn Yaḥyā al-Khathʿamī narrated from Abī ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام that he said:

The Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم used to perform the Maghrib salat, and a clan from the Anṣār called Banū Salimah would pray with him. Their homes were at a distance of half a mile, then they would return to their homes while they could still see the places where their arrows fell.

key_terms.الْأَنْصَارِ: the Anṣār, the Helpers of Madinah
key_terms.الْمَغْرِبَ: the Maghrib salat, the sunset prayer
key_terms.بَنُو سَلِمَةَ: Banū Salimah, a clan among the Anṣār
key_terms.مَوَاضِعَ سِهَامِهِمْ: the places of their arrows, meaning visible ground marks in remaining light

ai.seo_question: How early was the Maghrib prayer performed by the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم?
ai.summary: This hadith reports the practice of the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم in performing the Maghrib salat and describes how Banū Salimah from the Anṣār prayed with him and then returned home before darkness fully set in. It indicates the early timing of Maghrib and preserves a practical description of the visible light remaining after the prayer.
